skill.name: convex-performance-audit
skill.description: Audits Convex applications for slow queries, write contention, subscription cost, and function limit problems. It guides focused fixes using code evidence and runtime signals.
skill.summary: Finds Convex performance bottlenecks and recommends targeted fixes.
skill.author: get-convex

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples that use Convex ctx.db APIs or mention reference paths. Two findings are confirmed: the skill asks agents to run npx Convex CLI commands, including an unpinned latest package fallback. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs agents to run Convex CLI commands with npx.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation, show the exact command, and prefer the project-pinned Convex CLI when available.

remediation.issue: The fallback command uses npx -y convex@latest, which auto-installs the latest package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the CLI version or ask users to install or approve the package before execution.

content.value_statement: Convex apps can become slow when queries, subscriptions, or writes grow without clear signals. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a focused performance audit.
actual_capabilities: Routes symptoms to hot-path, OCC, subscription, or function-budget guidance.
Uses Convex insights, dashboard signals, and code paths to scope an audit.
Identifies unbounded reads, broad filters, large payloads, and costly subscriptions.
Suggests indexes, digest tables, batched mutations, and point-in-time reads when justified.
Checks sibling readers and writers for repeated performance patterns.
Defines verification steps for behavior, read volume, and invalidation changes.
limitations: It does not replace production monitoring or load testing.
It depends on access to application code and available Convex signals.
It recommends larger migrations only after measured evidence.
It does not provide general Convex setup or authentication guidance.

use_cases.title: Plan a Performance Triage
use_cases.description: Classify slow flows and choose the smallest safe fix.

use_cases.title: Reduce Query and Write Cost
use_cases.description: Find unbounded reads, broad filters, no-op writes, and contention in Convex functions.

use_cases.title: Improve Reactive UI Responsiveness
use_cases.description: Review subscriptions and point-in-time reads for pages that do not need live updates.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Slow Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Convex feature for performance. Start by identifying the user flow, involved functions, tables read, and tables written.

prompt_templates.title: Review Read Amplification
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hot-path rules to inspect this query path. Flag unbounded reads, JS filtering, large documents, and missing index opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Subscription Cost
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this page for subscription cost. Compare live reactivity with point-in-time reads, and preserve freshness where users need it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Cross-Path Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration-safe performance plan for this Convex area. Include sibling functions, rollout order, verification, and risks before editing.

output_examples.input: A dashboard loads slowly and Convex insights shows high documents read.
output: Classifies the issue as hot-path read amplification.
Recommends bounded indexed reads before digest tables.
Adds verification for same results and lower read volume.

output_examples.input: A collaborative page has frequent OCC conflicts during voting.
output: Identifies the shared counter as a contention point.
Suggests splitting the hot document or scheduling secondary work.
Checks sibling writers before closing the audit.

output_examples.input: A report page uses live subscriptions, but data changes hourly.
output: Compares live subscriptions with point-in-time reads.
Keeps reactivity only where users need fresh updates.
Defines UI and dashboard checks for lower subscription cost.

best_practices: Start from measured signals, then inspect code when signals are missing.
Keep simple scans when data is small and no hot path is proven.
Verify behavior and performance changes before closing the audit.
anti_patterns: Applying digest tables without evidence of repeated read cost.
Switching live subscriptions to point-in-time reads when users need fresh updates.
Fixing one function while sibling readers or writers keep the same bottleneck.

faq.question: Does this skill run Convex commands automatically?
faq.answer: It may suggest Convex CLI insights. Users should approve commands before execution.

faq.question: Can it fix code directly?
faq.answer: Yes, when the requested scope is clear and the changes are local.

faq.question: Does it require production access?
faq.answer: No. It can audit code only, but runtime signals improve accuracy.

faq.question: Will it always recommend indexes?
faq.answer: No. It recommends indexes only when they reduce a real hot-path scan.

faq.question: Can it help with OCC conflicts?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers broad read sets, hot documents, no-op writes, and scheduled follow-up work.

faq.question: Is it only for React apps?
faq.answer: No. It includes React subscription patterns, but backend Convex functions are also covered.
